# Sirach 22 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 22 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 13

---

## Disagreement 001 — 22:1-2 dung/filth imagery intensity
**Verse:** 22:1-2
**EMET:** "stone covered-with-filth" / "dung of-the-dunghill"
**LOGOS:** "stone covered with filth" / "dung of a dunghill"
**PNEUMA:** "stone smeared with dung" / "pile of manure on the heap"
**Issue:** PNEUMA intensifies the imagery ("smeared with dung," "pile of manure") where the Greek is more restrained. The comparison should be gross but not gratuitously so.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: retains "filth" and "dung of a dunghill" — preserving the coarseness without amplification.

---

## Disagreement 002 — 22:5 "bold-one / brazen / shameless"
**Verse:** 22:5
**EMET:** "The-bold-one"
**LOGOS:** "A brazen woman"
**PNEUMA:** "A shameless woman"
**Issue:** θρασεῖα — "bold/brazen." EMET leaves gender implicit; the context makes it feminine. LOGOS and PNEUMA both supply "woman." SOPHIA follows PNEUMA's "shameless" as most readable.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A shameless woman."

---

## Disagreement 003 — 22:6 "discourse out-of-season / speech at an unseasonable time / speaking at the wrong moment"
**Verse:** 22:6
**EMET:** "A-discourse out-of-season"
**LOGOS:** "A speech at an unseasonable time"
**PNEUMA:** "Speaking at the wrong moment"
**Issue:** μουσικὰ ἐν πένθει — "music in grief/mourning." The second line uses "music" as the vehicle of comparison. All three agents handle this differently in the first line. SOPHIA: "A word at the wrong time."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A word at the wrong time is like music at a funeral."

---

## Disagreement 004 — 22:7 "glues-together / gluing together"
**Verse:** 22:7
**EMET:** "like one-who-glues-together a-potsherd"
**LOGOS:** "like gluing together broken pottery"
**PNEUMA:** "like trying to glue a shattered pot back together"
**Issue:** ὁ κολλῶν ὄστρακον — "the one gluing a potsherd." PNEUMA adds "shattered" and "trying to." LOGOS and EMET are closer to the Greek. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "like gluing broken pottery back together."

---

## Disagreement 005 — 22:8 "recounts an account / tells something important"
**Verse:** 22:8
**EMET:** "Whoever-recounts an-account to a-fool"
**LOGOS:** "Whoever recounts a matter to a fool"
**PNEUMA:** "Tell something important to a fool"
**Issue:** The Greek lacks any qualifier meaning "important." PNEUMA's addition is interpretive. SOPHIA drops the relative clause for smoother English.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Whoever tells something important to a fool" — retaining PNEUMA's idiomatic smoothness but noting the interpretive nature.

---

## Disagreement 006 — 22:9 three-part mourning structure
**Verse:** 22:9
**EMET:** Full three-part structure: "Weep / Weep / Weep more-gently"
**LOGOS:** Full three-part structure
**PNEUMA:** Full three-part structure but adds "at least the dead are at rest"
**Issue:** All agents preserve the structure. PNEUMA adds "at least" which is interpretive. SOPHIA keeps the lean parallel structure.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: Preserves the three-part structure without additions: "Weep for the dead... weep for the fool... Weep more gently for the dead."

---

## Disagreement 007 — 22:11 "go-not to / do not visit / don't go looking for"
**Verse:** 22:11
**EMET:** "go-not to one-who-is-without-understanding"
**LOGOS:** "do not visit one without understanding"
**PNEUMA:** "don't go looking for company among the senseless"
**Issue:** PNEUMA's expansion ("looking for company") goes beyond the Greek. LOGOS's "visit" is appropriately literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "do not keep company with one without understanding."

---

## Disagreement 008 — 22:13 "lump-of-iron / block of iron / lump"
**Verse:** 22:13
**EMET:** "a-lump-of-iron"
**LOGOS:** "a lump of iron"
**PNEUMA:** "a block of iron"
**Issue:** μάζαν σιδηρᾶν — "iron mass/lump." Both "lump" and "block" work. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a lump of iron."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 22:14 "wooden-beams / beams of timber / beams lashed"
**Verse:** 22:14
**EMET:** "wooden-beams bound-together in a-building"
**LOGOS:** "beams of timber bound together in a building"
**PNEUMA:** "beams lashed together inside a building"
**Issue:** ξύλα δεδεμένα ἐν οἰκοδομῇ — "wood/timbers bound in a building." PNEUMA's "inside" is added. All are defensible. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Like wooden beams bound together in a building."

---

## Disagreement 010 — 22:16-18 near-repetition of verses
**Verses:** 22:15, 22:18
**EMET/LOGOS/PNEUMA:** All note that vv. 15 and 18 seem nearly identical in Vaticanus.
**Issue:** The repetition is present in the Greek text. Some MSS omit one. SOPHIA retains both as they appear in Vaticanus but notes the textual issue.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: Both verses retained; slight verbal variation introduced to reflect minor MS differences.

---

## Disagreement 011 — 22:20 listing of friend-destroying acts
**Verse:** 22:20
**EMET:** "insult and arrogance and disclosure of-a-secret and a-treacherous-blow"
**LOGOS:** "insult and arrogance and betrayal of a secret and a treacherous blow"
**PNEUMA:** "insults, arrogance, betraying a secret, a treacherous attack"
**Issue:** "Disclosure" (EMET) vs "betrayal" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) for ἀποκάλυψις — "uncovering/revelation." "Betrayal" is more idiomatic and captures the relational gravity.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "betraying a confidence" — slightly stronger than "secret."

---

## Disagreement 012 — 22:27 "sealed-seal / sealed lock / seal"
**Verse:** 22:25
**EMET:** "a-sealed-seal upon my-lips"
**LOGOS:** "a seal upon my lips"
**PNEUMA:** "a seal on my lips"
**Issue:** σφραγῖδα σφραγῖδος — "seal of a seal," a doubling for emphasis. EMET preserves the doubling; LOGOS and PNEUMA reduce. SOPHIA uses "sealed lock" to capture the intensified sense.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a sealed lock upon my lips."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 22:27 "ignorances / folly / acts of folly"
**Verse:** 22:27
**EMET:** "in-my-ignorances"
**LOGOS:** "in my ignorances"
**PNEUMA:** "in my foolishness"
**Issue:** ἐν ταῖς ἀγνοίαις μου — "in my ignorances," plural. The plural is significant — acts of unknowing sin. PNEUMA's singular "foolishness" loses the plural. SOPHIA uses "acts of folly" to preserve the plural while being more natural.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "in my acts of folly."
